> **What this case shows** — physical-activity accelerometry rests on two metrics: **ENMO** (how far
> the acceleration magnitude sits *above* 1 g) and **MAD** (how much it *varies* within an epoch). The
> ecosystem's ENMO was already certified against **GGIR**, the field-standard package — but it had no
> MAD. This case introduces a **newly-authored op**, `computeMAD`, completing the pair. On a real
> ~62-minute free-living hand-accelerometer recording it reproduces `GGIR::g.applymetrics` MAD to
> **machine precision** (max |diff| ~**5e-14 g**, r = **1.0**) across all **749** epochs — and the MAD
> traces a real movement profile (5–1222 mg, mean 232 mg).

::: {.callout-tip title="The recipe you'll learn"}
**Workflow** — `computeMAD(accel, sampling_rate, epoch_sec)` → per-epoch mean amplitude deviation.
**Way of thinking** — ENMO and MAD answer different questions of the same signal: *elevation* vs
*variation* of the magnitude. MAD is robust to a static orientation offset (it subtracts the epoch
mean), so it behaves well on uncalibrated or gravity-contaminated data where ENMO can drift.
**Ecosystem usage** — `PhysioWearable::computeMAD()` alongside `computeENMO()` — both GGIR-certified.
:::

## Proposition

On real PAMAP2 hand-accelerometer data (749 epochs of 5 s at 100 Hz), `computeMAD` reproduces
`GGIR::g.applymetrics` MAD to machine precision (max |diff| ~5e-14 g, r = 1.0); the recording's MAD
ranges 5–1222 mg (mean 232 mg).

## Question & goal

**The question is a gap and its fidelity: the ecosystem had GGIR-certified ENMO but no MAD — can we
author the complementary gravity-robust movement metric and reproduce the field-standard GGIR exactly
on real free-living data?** The goal is to introduce `computeMAD`, certify it against GGIR epoch by
epoch, and read off the movement profile.

## Challenge & approach

MAD per epoch is mean(|r − mean(r)|), where r = √(x²+y²+z²) is the sample vector magnitude. We compute
it per non-overlapping 5 s epoch and check it against `GGIR::g.applymetrics(..., metrics2do$do.mad)` on
the identical signal.

```
PAMAP2 hand accel (x,y,z @ 100 Hz) → r = √(x²+y²+z²) → per 5 s epoch: MAD = mean(|r − mean(r)|)
                    vs GGIR::g.applymetrics MAD (same signal) → machine precision (5e-14 g, r = 1.0)
                    749 epochs; MAD 5–1222 mg (mean 232 mg) — a real free-living movement profile
```

## Data

**PAMAP2 Physical Activity Monitoring dataset (UCI/PhysioNet)**: subject **101**, hand-worn IMU
accelerometer (x, y, z in g at 100 Hz), a ~62-minute free-living recording — the same git-tracked
signal the [ENMO free-living case](../adl-freeliving-pamap2/index.qmd) uses. Details in
[`artifacts/data_sources.json`](artifacts/data_sources.json).

The newly-authored op matches GGIR at every epoch, and the MAD traces a physical movement profile.

## Conclusion

`computeMAD` completes the ENMO+MAD pair — the ecosystem now has both field-standard accelerometer
movement metrics, each GGIR-certified — and it is exact: bit-for-bit against GGIR across a full
free-living recording. The transferable takeaway: **ENMO and MAD are complements, not substitutes.
Report MAD when a static orientation offset or imperfect calibration would bias ENMO, and use both to
characterize movement by its elevation and its variation.**

## Open questions

- MAD-based physical-activity intensity cut-points (Vähä-Ypyä et al. 2015 give sedentary/light/moderate/
  vigorous MAD thresholds); classifying intensity by MAD and cross-checking against the ENMO cut-points
  on the same recording would turn the two metrics into a cross-validated activity layer. *Documented,
  not escalated.*

## Using this in your own analysis

| Step | Function | Package |
|---|---|---|
| Mean amplitude deviation (variation) | `computeMAD()` | PhysioWearable |
| Euclidean norm minus one (elevation) | `computeENMO()` | PhysioWearable |
| Intensity bouts / cut-points | `classifyBouts()` | PhysioWearable |

**Choosing the parameters.**

- **epoch_sec** — aggregation window (here 5 s, the GGIR default); shorter epochs resolve brief bouts,
  longer epochs smooth the profile.
- **sampling_rate** — required when `epoch_sec` is set (here 100 Hz).
- **unit** — `"g"` (default) or `"mg"`; MAD is a physical quantity, so the unit matters for cut-points.

**The recipe, copy-runnable:**

```r
library(PhysioWearable)

mad <- computeMAD(accel, sampling_rate = 100, epoch_sec = 5)   # per-epoch MAD (g)
# reproduces GGIR::g.applymetrics MAD to machine precision; pair with computeENMO().
```

**Auditing the numbers.** Every value on this page traces to
[`artifacts/mad_summary.csv`](artifacts/mad_summary.csv), and [`audit.py`](audit.py) re-checks the
bit-exact GGIR agreement (max |diff|, correlation), the epoch count, the mean/max/min MAD, and the
honestly-noted scope (newly-authored op; machine-precision; MAD a physical quantity complementary to
ENMO).
